question:
The ratio of the radii of two concentric circles is \(1:3.\) If \(\overline{AC}\) is a diameter of the larger circle, \(\overline{BC}\) is a chord of the larger circle that is tangent to the smaller circle, and \(AB=12,\) then the radius of the larger circle is

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_12_Q11_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Let \(O\) be the common center and \(T\) the point where \(BC\) touches the smaller circle. Joining \(O\) to \(T\) connects the smaller radius to the triangle formed by \(A,B,C\).

A radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent, so \(OT\perp BC\). In the larger circle, a perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects that chord. Thus \(T\) is the midpoint of \(BC\). Also, \(O\) is the midpoint of the diameter \(AC\).

Therefore \(OT\) joins the midpoints of two sides of triangle \(ABC\). By the triangle midsegment theorem,
\[
OT=\frac{AB}{2}=\frac{12}{2}=6.
\]
This is the smaller radius. Since the radii are in the ratio \(1:3\), the larger radius is \(3\cdot6=\boxed{18}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
